task.description: Independently re-verified ELIXIR-DEV's REQ-233 claims (32->2 parity-phrasing occurrences, 2 divergence lines byte-identical, .zig citations 41==41, comment/moduledoc/test-assertion-only diff, one test-assertion change), and decided TEST-DESIGNER routing.

findings: Re-ran grep -roE '...' independently: 2 occurrences remain (execution_error.ex:7, capability_gate.ex:97). Confirmed both are the claimed exceptions: execution_error.ex:7 is the required-verbatim divergence line ('unlike R-Co's own'), and capability_gate.ex:97's 'parity' hit is inside a real on-disk citation to lib/letflow/design/req172-wasm-host-api-write-path-and-parity-suite.md (verified filename exists). Neither is a rationalized skip.

Re-ran divergence-line grep and diffed each line's full text against main via git show: execution_error.ex:7 and pin_resolver.ex:141 are byte-identical to main. Genuine preservation, not just presence.
Re-summed grep -c '\.zig' across the 13 files on both main and the feature branch: 41 == 41, confirmed independently.
git diff --stat main...feature branch shows only the 13 named lib/ files, test/letflow/engine/schemas_test.exs, and the two handoff JSONs -- no scope creep.

Read the full lib/ diff end to end and isolated all added lines: every one lives inside a moduledoc/typedoc/comment block. No def/defp signature, @spec, case/cond branch, or struct/type shape line was touched anywhere in the 13 files. Spot-checked 6 rewritten sentences (execution_error.ex open-union rationale, variable_schema.ex N+1-avoidance and INV-7 parameterization comments, pin_resolver.ex resolved_id anti-pattern reasoning, lua/platform.ex capability_matrix self-reference, wasm/host_api.ex uuid asymmetry note) against the actual code below each -- all state real, checkable technical reasons (an actual @typedoc union shape, an actual query call site, an actual @capability_matrix module attribute), not invented plausible-sounding text.

schemas_test.exs change: read before/after. The old test asserted a substring that WAS the exact retired phrase ('matching R-Co's own tokens.status strings exactly') -- the test existed only to check that TokenRecord's moduledoc documents the lowercase-casing choice as deliberate. The new assertions check for the replacement phrasing that carries the same intent (a fixed convention, distinguished from Task.status's opposite casing) verbatim against the rewritten moduledoc. This is a mechanical consequence of the phrasing retirement, not a coverage loss -- the thing being tested (that the casing split is documented as deliberate, not an oversight) is unchanged and still asserted.

mix unavailable in this review environment (no toolchain) -- compile/test claims not independently re-run; relying instead on the diff-based proof above, which is decisive for a comment/moduledoc/test-assertion-only change: no code path could have changed to affect compile or runtime behavior.
result.test_designer_routing: SKIP, per REQ-232 precedent. No new behavior, branch, or error path was introduced anywhere in the 13 lib/ files -- confirmed directly by diff inspection, not merely claimed. The one test-assertion change in schemas_test.exs is a mechanical rename of an assertion string tracking retired wording it existed to check, not new coverage or a coverage gap -- appropriately made by ELIXIR-DEV's own hand rather than needing TEST-DESIGNER.
